audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: every Dawkins 1916 sentence in the record (secs. 60, 72, 73, 117, 184, 222) is verbatim in the held archive.org scanned text at the lines given above, and both Karatsareas 2011 passages are at printed pp. 236 and 239 as the adjudicated locator says. The deciding source is the primary reference description of the dialect (Dawkins, fieldwork 1909-11), which for a language dispersed in 1924 remains the authoritative data source; the LEXICAL verdict (inherited Greek free accent with morphological shifts and enclisis effects) is what those passages presuppose and is not in doubt for a Modern Greek dialect, and the one open paper fetched sources now (Spyropoulos et al. 2016) likewise presupposes contrastive final/penult/antepenult noun stress. sources.citation: Spyropoulos, Vassilios, Anthi Revithiadou & Giorgos Markopoulos. 2016. Harmony as a cue for the transition from fusion to agglutination. Selected Papers on Theoretical and Applied Linguistics (ISTAL) 21: 447-457 (running headers). doi:10.26262/istal.v21i0.5241
sources.quote: p. 448: 'the process is stress-sensitive since it affects mainly words stressed on the (ante)penultimate syllable. However, a stressed final vowel can be a trigger ...'; p. 449 fn. 7: 'the position of stress seems to affect the distribution of the inflectional paradigms, since nouns stressed on the final syllable tend to be inflected according to the agglutinative pattern.' Presupposes contrastive final/penult/antepenult stress across Cappadocian nouns; no accent rule stated.
sources.locator: p. 448 (sec. on properties of vowel assimilation) and p. 449 fn. 7
